item.title: A10 Bullsmoor Lane / M25 Junction 25 – recurring gridlock, 8th September
item.description:
Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing about the recurring congestion on the A10 Great Cambridge Road between Bullsmoor Lane and M25 Junction 25. I use this route regularly and have been caught in severe congestion here many times. The short distance between the traffic lights north of Bullsmoor Lane and the junction itself means queues can quickly back up and block Bullsmoor. If there is an accident or disruption around M25 Junction 25, the whole area can become completely gridlocked. From personal experience, being repeatedly trapped in this is genuinely soul-destroying. When this happens, driver behaviour also deteriorates. I regularly see vehicles jumping red lights, entering the yellow box without a clear exit and blocking other traffic. While drivers are responsible for their own actions, once this starts, an already serious problem rapidly becomes worse. I would be grateful if consideration could be given to: * Reviewing the coordination of the traffic lights around Bullsmoor and the northbound A10. * Better monitoring and a coordinated response, including police or traffic officers when serious incidents cause the area to become gridlocked. * A longer-term review of the capacity of M25 Junction 25 and whether a more substantial solution is required, such as an A10 flyover or a cut-through (“hamburger”) roundabout. I appreciate that major infrastructure changes are neither simple nor inexpensive, but this is a recurring problem that I believe needs more than adjustments to traffic-light timings. Given that this issue involves both the TfL-managed A10 and National Highways’ M25 Junction 25, I am sending this to both organisations and would welcome a coordinated response. I have attached a map highlighting the two locations where I regularly see the problem developing. Kind regards, Yiltan Kemal

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Great Cambridge Road, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
